sentences.text: Sinornithoides was a small dinosaur about one meter long that likely ate invertebrates and other small prey. As a member of the troodontid family, it possessed sickle-claws, raptorial hands, and a high encephalization quotient indicating advanced behavior and keen senses.
Its skull contained four premaxillary teeth and about twenty-three maxillary teeth.
The holotype specimen preserves a furcula and a basket consisting of fifteen pairs of gastralia.
The sickle claw on the second toe of Sinornithoides is relatively large and long compared to other troodontids.
In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the body length of Sinornithoides at 1.1 meters and its weight at 2.5 kilograms.
The generic name Sinornithoides means "Chinese bird form," derived from Latin and Greek roots referencing its bird-like build.
The specific name youngi honors the paleontologist Yang Zhongjian.
A Chinese-Canadian expedition discovered the remains of Sinornithoides near Huamuxiao in the Ordos Basin of Inner Mongolia in 1988.
The species Sinornithoides youngi was named and described in 1993 or 1994 by Dale Russell and Dong Zhiming.
The holotype specimen IVPP V9612 is an almost complete, articulated skeleton missing only the roof of the skull and some vertebrae.
The holotype specimen represents a subadult individual.
In 1994, Sinornithoides was assigned to the family Troodontidae.
Despite the lack of sufficient comparative fossil material to identify diagnostic traits, Sinornithoides was assigned to the Troodontidae family.
A 2012 analysis by Turner, Makovicky, and Norell shows a possible position for Sinornithoides in the evolutionary tree of Paraves.
Sinornithoides lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Aptian or Albian stages around 113 million years ago, in Inner Mongolia, China.
The fossil record for Sinornithoides spans the Albian stage from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
